title: How BMS is organised: from the President to the Udyog Prabhari
author: Editorial Desk
summary: A short tour of the Karya Karini and its tiers.
body:
For a new karyakarta, the structure of the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh can seem complex. How does a union in one factory connect to a federation, a State and the national body? Who decides what? Here is a simple map, based on the Karya Karini page of this website, together with some background on how the organisation came to take this shape.

## A short history of the structure

BMS was founded on **23 July 1955** in Bhopal under Dattopant Thengadi. According to the BMS "At a Glance" page, it began with no unions, no members, no office and no funds. For its first years it had no formal organisational structure; it set up State units and trained young worker cadres, and in **1967** it held its first All India Conference in Delhi, at which a national executive was elected. At that time it reported 541 affiliated unions.

Today, the BMS website says it has unions in all 44 industries classified by the Ministry of Labour and claims a membership of almost one crore across all States, with more than 5,000 affiliated unions. The figures are the organisation's own claim. Government verification exercises have placed BMS second among central trade unions in 1984, with 12,11,355 members, and first in 1996, with 31,17,324 members on a reckoning date of 31 December 1989; it retained first place in the 2002 verification. The size has made a clear structure necessary, with each level doing a defined job.

## The national team

The national team is the top of the structure. As listed on the Karya Karini page, it includes:

- **President:** presides over the National Executive and represents BMS nationally.
- **Vice Presidents:** seven, sharing the national responsibilities.
- **General Secretary:** the chief executive office-bearer; there is only one.
- **Secretaries:** six national secretaries.
- **National office posts:** Organising Secretary, Deputy Organising Secretary, Finance Secretary, Office Secretary and Karyalay Pramukh.

The head office is **Dattopant Thengadi Bhawan**, 27 Deendayal Upadhyay Marg, New Delhi. The numbers in each category can change from term to term. The team elected in February 2026, for example, had twenty national office-bearers: a President, a General Secretary, a Finance Secretary, an Organising Secretary, a Joint Organising Secretary, an Office Secretary, seven Vice Presidents and seven Secretaries. The point for a new karyakarta is that the posts are elected, they come from different States and sectors, and no single person carries the organisation.

## Zones

To make a national organisation manageable, BMS groups States into zones. Seven **Zonal Organising Secretaries** look after zones such as the Northern, North Central, North Eastern and Eastern, South and South Central, Western, and East Central zones, supported by Assistant Organising Secretaries. A zonal secretary works as a link: he visits States, helps in resolving internal difficulties, supports the formation of new units and carries the experience of the States to the national leadership. For a worker in a district, the zonal secretary is the nearest face of the national office.

## Sectors

Besides the territorial structure there is a structure by industry. **Udyog Prabharis** are in charge of five groups: the unorganised, private, public, government and social security sectors. Each Udyog Prabhari connects the national office with the industry federations in his group. The reason for this is practical. The problems of a coal miner, a bank employee and a domestic worker have almost nothing in common, and the same is true of the laws and negotiating bodies that govern them. An Udyog Prabhari who follows one group of industries can help federations to prepare their demands, take part in the relevant negotiating bodies and ensure that the national position matches what the workers in that industry need.

## Federations and States

Under the national centre there are **38 federations** by industry, and State and district units by region. The two structures meet at the level of the local union. A worker in a factory joins a local union, which is affiliated to an industry federation (for instance, one for steel or cement) and, at the same time, to the State and national BMS. The industry line deals with wages, service conditions and negotiations specific to the industry. The territorial line deals with local organisation, State governments, and issues that cross industries, such as State minimum wages or the implementation of a welfare board.

A simple example makes this clear. A worker in a steel plant in a given State belongs to a plant union. That union is a member of the steel federation, which negotiates wage agreements at the industry level, and also of the State unit, which raises matters with the State Government. The same worker's union may also take part in a joint campaign led by the national office on a matter such as a Labour Code.

## How decisions are made

BMS decisions are taken in meetings of its elected bodies. The national executive and the Kendriya Karya Samiti (the central working committee) meet at intervals to adopt resolutions. For example, the 159th meeting of the Kendriya Karya Samiti was held in Bhopal from 22 to 24 August 2025, and adopted resolutions that included a call for the Wage Code and the Social Security Code to be implemented immediately. Meetings of this type show the working of the structure: the resolution reflects the discussion of representatives from States and sectors, and is then taken up by the office-bearers in their dealings with the Government.

## Elections

BMS has a regular cycle of elections. Its triennial national conference elects the national office-bearers for a three-year term. In February 2026, at the conference at Puri in Odisha, **S. Mallesham** was elected President and **Surendra Kumar Pandey** General Secretary for the 2026-29 term; according to the BMS website, the conference had over 2,500 delegates from all States and Union Territories. We report on that in a later post.

## What a new karyakarta should do

1. Find out which local union and which federation your workplace belongs to.
2. Learn the name of your district and State office-bearers and the Udyog Prabhari for your sector.
3. Attend the meetings of your union and read its resolutions, since this is where the structure becomes real.
4. When you take up a problem, send it first through the union and the federation concerned, and only then to the State and national levels. Matters that are raised at the correct level are solved faster.
5. Remember the common purpose: the structure is not there to create posts, but to carry the worker's voice from the workplace to the place where decisions are made.
